A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NG-SM multi-view latent-variable model. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, manifold-learning, reconstruction, missing-data and runtime experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds multi-view classification, image reconstruction and supplementary analyses in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The spectral-density model, mixture-wise RFF construction, two-step sampler, variational objective and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure. NG-MV-RFLVM is renamed NG-MVLVM. Corrections to the derived kernel expression do not establish a change to the implemented learning procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds evaluations on MNIST–SVHN paired digit images, MOVIES keyword/actor views and CORA content/citation views. It also adds quantitative image reconstruction on MNIST, CIFAR and both MNIST–SVHN views. Existing coverage, including single-view experiments moved to the appendix, is retained.

E2.justification: The runtime comparison labels a comparator MV-GPLVM in v1 Figure 5 and MV-NGPLVM in v2 Figure 3; the latter is explicitly identified as the Gibbs-kernel variant. This changes the reported comparator membership, without establishing a rerun. Retained classification tables keep their comparator sets, and new benchmarks reuse existing methods.

E3.justification: Table 4 substantially revises reported dataset configurations: BRIDGES changes from 2,000 samples/two dimensions to 214/four, NEWSGROUPS from 20,000 samples to 2,752, and CIFAR from 32×32 to 20×20 pixels. Other dimensions and channel counts also change. New experiments introduce neural-network classification and image-MSE evaluation protocols. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds runtime sensitivity across mixture counts and feature dimensions in Figure 7, extending the existing representation-quality sensitivity analysis. Figure 10 adds qualitative clustering analysis on three datasets. Existing view-count, rotated-MNIST and missing-data analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report results over five experiments with means and standard deviations, including runtime uncertainty. New result tables follow that practice. No changed run count, seed policy, confidence-interval procedure or significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: New Tables 9–10 substantially extend reported classification and reconstruction results: for example, OURS achieves 93.13±0.84% MNIST–SVHN KNN accuracy and 0.023±0.0004 MNIST reconstruction MSE. New timing and clustering results are also reported. All numerical entries in the original two classification tables are retained; the additions are not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 removes a duplicated correlation factor from the kernel cross terms in v1 Equations 35–39, yielding v2 Equations 36–40 consistent with the stated covariance block. Appendix C.6 expands the spectral-norm derivation and adds Lemma 4 with a proof that a real symmetric matrix squared is PSD. Main theorem statements and the final approximation bound remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: expressive universal kernel approximation, efficient differentiable RFF inference and superior unified representations. Renaming the model and adding supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix E identifies the lack of explicit cross-view dependency modeling as a limitation for structured dependencies and proposes interaction terms. New reconstruction and clustering results receive additional interpretations. Appendix D.4.4 also discusses gains over MV-NGPLVM, although that comparator is absent from its Table 9.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code access link for the proposed method, hardware specifications, clarification that channel simulations introduce no explicit additive noise, and view dimensions/source links for new datasets. Existing default hyperparameters and baseline implementation links remain. These additions expand documentation without establishing implementation changes.

R1.justification: The bibliography removes peripheral entries, including Casale et al. (2018), Sutter et al. (2020, 2021) and Yuan et al. (2024). Substantive positioning relative to VAEs, GPLVMs, spectral kernels and RFF methods remains largely unchanged; citation-style and publication-metadata updates are presentational.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: background discussion moves into the introduction, single-view evaluation moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix D.4.1, and runtime evaluation moves into the main experiments. Appendices are reorganized around notation, theory and expanded experiments, alongside method-name standardization and rewritten explanatory passages.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column NeurIPS layout. Existing figures and tables are relocated and reformatted; synthetic-result panels are rearranged and the runtime plot gains a zoom inset. New displays include a graphical model, notation table, timing heatmap, clustering visualization and two result tables.

improvement.justification: Tables 9–10 broaden validation beyond the original benchmarks, while the kernel correction, expanded proofs and code/hardware disclosures improve checkability. These gains are tempered by unreconciled dataset descriptions and reporting errors: channel counts still conflict across sections, and Figure 10 appears to interchange the BRIDGES and NEWSGROUPS labels. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
